focus.jbig: Relief rally cooling · AI/chip rotation day 2 · Qualcomm −10% · oil −8% · VIX ~17 · 12 setups boarded
focus.jtag: The post-election bounce is fading as chip and data-center names keep selling; Dow futures hold up (~+0.5%) while Nasdaq futures lag (~−0.7%). Oil collapsed ~8% on Iran peace hopes, pulling WTI toward ~$88. The scanner boarded 6 Type A gaps (LNC, UBER, SMCI, WRBY, GIL, BDX, TRMB) and 5 Type C breakouts (ICE, RSP, JEPI, PG, XLF)
focus.jnote: Day two of the post-election tape is a rotation, not an all-clear. A rotation trade fueled by the US midterm elections entered a second day, with previously unfavored markets and economically sensitive stocks outperforming at the expense of chipmakers. Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 0.5% while S&P 500 futures were little changed, and a chip-giant ETF dropped more than 2% premarket on fears the Democrats' sweep leads to tighter data-center regulation. The single-stock shock is Qualcomm: Qualcomm dropped 10.1% in premarket trading after falling short of Wall Street estimates for fourth-quarter smartphone chip sales on sluggish demand and declining Apple-related revenue. The clear relief is in oil: WTI crude fell $7.97, or 8.3%, to $88.12, as investors weighed the possibility that the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory could increase pressure on President Trump to end the conflict with Iran. Vol stayed contained — the VIX was 16.85 at 5:50am ET, up 1.51% from Wednesday's 16.60 close, and under its 8-day, 21-day and 200-day averages. Calmer than a week ago, but still a half-size tape with the chip complex in the crosshairs.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the non-chip breakouts and defensive gaps are the cleanest fit for a rotation tape. ICE (a held 3-session breakout), PG (a defensive staple), and the broad financial/equal-weight ETFs RSP, XLF and JEPI sit outside the data-center complex being sold today — economically sensitive stocks are outperforming at the expense of chipmakers. SMCI is the standout contradiction: the scanner tagged it bearish on a −4.5% gap, but it beat estimates of $1.20 by 50.83% and the reaction has been choppy — treat the bearish tag with caution. On a MILD-but-two-sided day every one is watch-only, A-grade and confirmed-at-9:35 only.
focus.notup: The bearish Type A names split between confirmed and conflicted. GIL is the cleanest bearish gap: Gildan lowered its 2026 revenue outlook to $5.4–$5.5 billion from $6.0–$6.2 billion and cut adjusted operating-margin guidance, and shares fell approximately 15.2% in premarket trading — a genuine guidance-cut gap-down. But LNC's bearish tag looks stale: Lincoln National reported Non-GAAP EPS of $2.01, beating estimates by $0.06, a beat that contradicts a short. Selling bear calls into a VIX-calm relief tape still invites a squeeze — treat each as watch-only.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? The oil crash and a VIX near 17 argue against RED — the worst geopolitical tail is deflating. But P(≥1% gap) ~35% sits right on the 35% trigger, which alone locks out GREEN, and a one-sided chip rout (Qualcomm −10%, data-center names down) keeps the tape rotating and two-sided. Every Type A gap here printed on light relative volume and several carry stale or conflicting bias tags. Half size, A-grade only, 7-DTE that clears today's data, and keep every spread clear of its name's next print.

Q3 productivity & Challenger job cuts today — the data cluster can whip rates and risk intraday just as the election premium bleeds out; a scheduled event any 7-DTE spread must clear.
